title: Research
text:
My research develops data-driven methods to make transportation systems safer, more efficient, and more equitable. Below are the main themes my lab works on; see Projects for active and past funded work, and Publications for the resulting papers.



Traffic Flow Theory & Control
Modeling and controlling traffic dynamics on freeways and arterials, including signal timing, ramp metering, and macroscopic/microscopic simulation of mixed human-driven and automated traffic.


Transportation Safety Analytics
Statistical and machine-learning methods for crash prediction, near-miss detection, and proactive safety management using naturalistic driving and infrastructure sensor data.


Connected & Automated Vehicles
Evaluating how connected-vehicle (CV) and automated-vehicle (AV) technologies affect network performance, safety, and energy use, with a focus on transition-period challenges.


Transit Equity & Accessibility
Measuring and improving access to public transit for underserved populations, combining GTFS data, land-use models, and accessibility metrics to inform service planning.


Freight & Urban Logistics
Understanding last-mile delivery, curb management, and freight network resilience in growing urban areas.


Applied Machine Learning for Mobility Data
Developing interpretable ML methods for large-scale mobility datasets, including probe-vehicle data, video-derived trajectories, and mobile-phone location data.





Methods & Tools
My group works with a mix of field data collection, high-fidelity traffic simulation (e.g., SUMO, VISSIM), statistical modeling, and machine learning. We prioritize reproducible, open-source workflows — code for select projects is available on GitHub.


Collaborations
I collaborate with researchers in computer science, urban planning, and public health, as well as with public-sector partners including [State DOT], [Regional Transit Agency], and [City Department of Transportation]. Get in touch about collaborating.

title: Teaching
text:
I aim to connect transportation engineering theory to problems students can see in their own cities — congestion, crashes, and unequal access to mobility. My courses combine foundational modeling with hands-on work using real traffic and transit datasets, so students leave able to apply these methods in practice, not just on exams.


Courses Taught




Fall 2024, Fall 2025 Undergraduate



Introduction to traffic flow theory, capacity analysis, and transportation planning fundamentals.




Spring 2025, Spring 2026 Graduate



Macroscopic and microscopic traffic modeling, calibration, and simulation using SUMO and VISSIM.




Fall 2025 Graduate Seminar



Statistical and machine-learning approaches to crash prediction and proactive safety management, with a semester-long applied project.
